transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Rosa Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Veridian Labs), Mohammed Khan (Head of AI), Diana Park (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Quick kickoff for POC scoping to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main goals: define success criteria (latency/throughput/accuracy/burn), workload sizing and benchmark plan, timelines for a 6-week pilot, and identify security/integration blockers. Agreed to run a Redwood-hosted dedicated benchmark first, then evaluate private/VPC if isolation required.

Topics Covered:
- Acceptance gates and metrics (p95 latency, throughput reqs, eval pass rate)
- Workload profile: sequence lengths, burst patterns, token burn
- Bench plan: harness, datasets, models, quantization variants
- Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted (fast), Dedicated (predictable throughput), Private/VPC (data residency)
- Security and compliance asks (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS)
- Timeline and next steps

Action Items (brief):
- Benchmark run (Redwood SE)
- Pilot pricing and reserved capacity options (AE)
- Customer to provide eval/prompts
- Security review scheduling

--- Transcript Body ---
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro, I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the deal. Rosa is our SE.
[00:08] Rosa Kim: hi all, Rosa here, i run performance and benchmarking for inference — mostly latency and throughput tradeoffs.
[00:13] Lena Ortiz: hey, lena — thanks. we want to make sure this pilot answers whether to run hosted or move to a private VPC down the line. our legal folks care about data residency and audit logs.
[00:25] Mohammed Khan: and from AI side, we have two main flows: short chat completions (avg 60 tokens) and longer summarizations (avg 700 tokens). peak qps expected ~120 req/s for chat bursts, sustained ~30 req/s.
[00:42] Diana Park: infra note: our infra team prefers dedicated GPU pools if cost is predictable, but we need optional on-prem route for regulated customers.
[00:51] Rosa Kim: got it. rough numbers are helpful. couple clarifying q's — what latency SLO are you targeting p95? and what's your token burn budget?
[01:00] Lena Ortiz: p95 under 250ms for chat is ideal, 1.2s for long summaries ok. budget — we want to keep cost under $X per 1M tokens, i'll put exact number in the doc after.
[01:12] Mohammed Khan: acceptance is also not just latency — the model must meet eval pass rate on our golden prompts: >95% accuracy on intent extraction, and hallucination rate <2% on factual QA.
[01:25] Samir Patel: good, so we have performance+quality gates. For the pilot we usually recommend a 3‑phase approach: discovery benchmarks (hosted or dedicated), small POC with routing rules and caching, then an optional private deployment if isolation required.
[01:38] Rosa Kim: quick note on caching — Redwood does prefix/KV cache which can drastically reduce cost for repeated context. depending on reuse rate, token burn can drop 30-60%. we'll want sample traffic to estimate hit rate.
[01:52] Speaker 1: (transcription glitch) i think you said key value cash?
[01:56] Rosa Kim: yes kv cache, sorry, the transcript sometimes says cash.
[02:00] Diana Park: security wise, we need KMS integration and SAML SSO + audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also, any EU data must remain in eu-region for those customers.
[02:12] Rosa Kim: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for on-premish networks; Hosted supports region pinning and retained logs but for full control Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[02:24] Mohammed Khan: can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private? our borderline use-case is we want isolated capacity but not full on-prem ops.
[02:32] Samir Patel: Sure — Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool in Redwood's managed infra, provides capacity isolation and predictable throughput, we handle infra ops; Private (VPC or on‑prem) hands networking and control to you — good for strict compliance. Dedicated is often the sweet spot for cost vs isolation.
[02:49] Lena Ortiz: for our compliance check we need encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and an audit trail with immutability — are those standard?
[02:58] Rosa Kim: yes, encryption in transit and at rest are standard. For immutable audit logs we can ship to your S3 bucket or to a log provider; Redwood Console has an audit export.
[03:10] Mohammed Khan: back to benchmarks, we want to test three model configs: full FP16 variant, 4-bit quantized, and a smaller family model as fallback. Also measure cold start for KV warming and steady state after cache warms.
[03:25] Rosa Kim: makes sense. We'll set up runs for: 1) steady throughput at 30 req/s for 1hr, 2) burst test to 120 qps for 2mins every 10mins for 4hrs, 3) long seq tests for average 700 tokens sequences with a subset of the eval set.
[03:41] Speaker 2: so the benchmark will produce p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, and cost per 1M tokens?
[03:47] Rosa Kim: correct, plus KV cache hit rate, and memory/kv cache pressure stats.
[03:52] Lena Ortiz: how does Redwood handle fallback when capacity is saturated? we can't have errors in production.
[03:58] Samir Patel: we have smart routing and fallback policies — policy can route to smaller model or another region, or queue requests. For production we advise canary + automatic fallback to a lower-cost model with a quality threshold.
[04:12] Diana Park: i'd like to see an example of the canary A/B rollout steps and rollback triggers.
[04:18] Rosa Kim: we'll include a standard rollback policy: p95 > threshold or error rate > 1% triggers rollback. Can define custom thresholds per route.
[04:27] Mohammed Khan: i worry about hallucination regressions with quantized models. do you run quantized evals?
[04:33] Rosa Kim: yes, we run prompt-based evals on quantized variants and flag regressions; Redwood Optimize offers recommendations and keeps a quality baseline. sometimes 4-bit can raise specific failure modes, we'll highlight those in the report.
[04:46] Speaker 1: (noise)
[04:48] Lena Ortiz: timeline — we want pilot results within two weeks, is that realistic?
[04:52] Samir Patel: two weeks is tight but possible if Veridian supplies eval set and traffic profile immediately. We'll run a fast dedicated benchmark (48–72 hours) then synthesize results. If everything looks good, pilot kickoff in week 3.
[05:04] Mohammed Khan: what's the expected burn rate during the benchmark? rough multiplier on production?
[05:09] Rosa Kim: depends on reuse. For chat with high reuse and KV cache, burn could be 0.6x nominal token spend; with long sequences it's closer to 1x–1.4x. We'll show a burn projection in the CSV.
[05:22] Diana Park: governance note — procurement needs an SLA appendix and incident response plan for Dedicated.
[05:29] Samir Patel: we can include our SLA terms and an incident response addendum in the contract draft.
[05:33] Rosa Kim: a couple of gotchas: if you want region-locked private deploy, there is an extra lead time — provisioning private VPC/on-prem nodes can take 2–4 weeks. Dedicated pools are usually 3–5 business days.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: good to know. We prefer to avoid a 4-week lead time if possible. So maybe start with Dedicated and then move to Private for specific regs.
[05:54] Mohammed Khan: acceptable. On metrics, we will set acceptance gates: chat p95 < 250ms, summary p95 < 1.2s, eval pass rate >95%, cost per 1M tokens within target, and KV cache hit >25% for chat.
[06:09] Rosa Kim: we'll instrument measuring for those exact gates and return a pass/fail matrix.
[06:13] Samir Patel: next up — who's owning the eval set delivery?
[06:17] Lena Ortiz: i'll own that, Mohammed will curate. we'll upload to the shared drive and drop link in the CRM.
[06:23] Rosa Kim: perfect. we'll need sample traffic profile as well: token distribution, seq length histogram, p95 qps spikes.
[06:30] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[06:32] Diana Park: for SSO, we use Okta. we need SAML metadata and SCIM for provisioning.
[06:38] Samir Patel: Okta and SCIM supported. We'll get our SSO integration guide to you.
[06:44] Rosa Kim: one more technical note: if you intend to use long-running KV caches across sessions, dedicated pools give more consistent cache residency. In hosted multi-tenant pools cache eviction is more dynamic. So for long conversation continuity, Dedicated helps.
[06:59] Mohammed Khan: that suggests Dedicated for chat-heavy product.
[07:03] Lena Ortiz: yes, and we can save on costs with caching.
[07:07] Speaker 1: (small laugh)
[07:09] Rosa Kim: on benchmarking we will also measure cold vs warmed tail latencies — sometimes p99 spikes on cold starts. We'll document warmup requirements.
[07:18] Diana Park: what about encryption keys — do you support customer-managed keys in Dedicated?
[07:23] Rosa Kim: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS; Private gives even more control.
[07:27] Mohammed Khan: can we test a quantized variant on Dedicated, see if hallucination crosses the threshold?
[07:33] Rosa Kim: yes, that's part of the plan. We'll run FP16 baseline, 4-bit quant, and smaller fallback.
[07:39] Lena Ortiz: any dependencies we should be aware of to start the benchmark?
[07:43] Samir Patel: just the eval set, traffic profile, and a contact for infra access if we need to set up VPC peering later.
[07:50] Mohammed Khan: risk: if Dedicated still has too high token burn, we might need to evaluate latency/cost trade-offs and possibly change to smaller model family.
[07:58] Rosa Kim: we'll present a decision matrix: latency vs cost vs accuracy across model/quantization/deploy modes.
[08:05] Samir Patel: for acceptance we'll produce a one-page verdict and a deeper appendix with CSVs and graphs.
[08:11] Diana Park: can we get a sample contract appendix for Dedicated pricing? procurement wants to see a ballpark.
[08:17] Samir Patel: yes i'll share a draft with reserved capacity tiers, burst pricing, and overage rates.
[08:23] Speaker 2: (typing)
[08:26] Rosa Kim: timeline recap — immediate actions: Samir sends pricing, Rosa schedules benchmark, Veridian provides eval and traffic by Fri 10/24. Bench runs 10/25–10/27, results on 10/28. Security deep-dive week of 10/27.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: that works, we'll prioritize the eval set.
[08:43] Mohammed Khan: small ask — include a sample prompt set that stresses our hallucination-sensitive flows; we need concrete examples.
[08:50] Rosa Kim: will do. We'll also include a sample prompt-to-metric mapping so you can see which prompts influence which gate.
[08:58] Lena Ortiz: are there any hidden costs we should watch for? storage of logs, long-term retention, extra egress?
[09:04] Samir Patel: good question. Logs export and long-retention are add-ons; egress between cloud regions may incur charges. We'll call these out in the pricing sheet.
[09:13] Diana Park: final: can we get a short one-page runbook for incident response during pilot? procurement wants that in the pack.
[09:20] Samir Patel: yes, we'll include a runbook and an on-call contact for the pilot window.
[09:25] Speaker 1: (background noise)
[09:27] Rosa Kim: ok i'll follow up with checklist and link to the benchmark harness repo.
[09:31] Samir Patel: thanks everyone, great alignment. we'll follow up via CRM and share calendar invites for the security deep-dive.
[09:38] Lena Ortiz: thanks all.
[09:40] Mohammed Khan: thanks, bye.
[09:42] Diana Park: bye.

End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels show generic 'Speaker 1/2/3' where audio overlapped; some technical terms were mis-transcribed (KV cache -> key value cash). We left those artifacts intact to preserve realism.

Bench plan summary (quick bulleted):
- Models: FP16 baseline, 4-bit quantized, smaller fallback
- Tests: steady 30 rps 1hr, burst 120 qps pattern for 4hrs, long-seq 700 tokens subset
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, cost/1M tokens, KV cache hit rate, cold vs warm tail, hallucination/regression per eval set
- Deploy modes evaluated: Hosted (fast start), Dedicated (predictable capacity, better cache residency), Private/VPC (regulatory, longer lead time)

Acceptance gates (agreed):
- Chat p95 < 250ms
- Summary p95 < 1.2s
- Eval pass rate > 95% on golden prompts
- Hallucination < 2% on QA set
- KV cache hit > 25% for chat flows or documented mitigation

Attachments referenced (links to be posted in CRM):
- Benchmark harness repo (private link)
- Pricing & reserved capacity sheet (Samir)
- Security pack & SSO guide (Redwood Security)
